chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
That which is not slaughtered with iron is not to be eaten.
ai.seo_question: What material must be used for slaughtering an animal for its meat to be permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar specifies that the instrument of slaughter must be made of iron (al-hadid), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the purity and durability of the cutting tool to ensure a clean cut and minimize animal suffering. While some schools accept other sharp materials, this narration highlights the preference for iron, linking the physical act of dhabh to the spiritual requirement of invoking God's name during the process.
